set.affordability_requirement: AHF 14 Affordability Threshold (NOFA Section IV.D): 100% of units (excluding manager unit) restricted to Low Income (80% AMI) and at least 15% of total units restricted to Extremely Low Income, for at least 55 years from completion under a County regulatory agreement (57 years from recording of the deed of trust); homelessness preference units count toward the 15% ELI threshold. The greater of 5% of low-income units or two units carry a preference for people experiencing homelessness at 30% AMI rents with tenant-based subsidies and a 60-day referral hold. MHSA/BHSA units serve behavioral health referrals at 30% AMI with PBVs or 20% AMI without. Senior studio and one-bedroom units may not assume rents above 50% AMI. The Board staff report describes typical project incomes of 30% to 60% AMI.
set.prevailing_wage_basis: AHF 14 NOFA Table 3 states Measure K and County impact fees do not trigger Davis-Bacon (the County requires certain other federal requirements); the NOFA states no state prevailing wage rule. State prevailing wage under Labor Code 1720 depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts; federal HOME or CDBG layered in from the Winter NOFA would trigger Davis-Bacon at 12+ HOME units or 8+ CDBG rehab units.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: AHF 14 NOFA (smcgov.org/media/159002) and Aug 25, 2026 Board item 26-679 confirm the $29,347,311 offer, $24,347,311 awards, May 20, 2026 deadline and caps. The $5,000,000 MHSA in AHF 14 was not awarded and is to be offered over the counter or in a later NOFA. Added the 100% low income and 15% ELI threshold and changed prevailing wage from true (uncited) to unclear.

reason: Material: affordability_requirement omitted the NOFA threshold of 100% low income units and at least 15% ELI units, and prevailing_wage_trigger true conflicts with the NOFA statement that Measure K does not trigger Davis-Bacon.

set.typical_award_size: No standalone fee waiver or deferral program for affordable housing, but the County Affordable Housing Impact Fee (Ordinance Code Chapter 5.154; rates and exemptions in Resolution 074532, Exhibit C) exempts new units rented or sold at affordable cost to very low, low or moderate income households under a deed restriction meeting County standards, housing for the elderly or disabled, and property eligible for the welfare exemption. Projects with an Area Standard Wage Participation Agreement get a 25% fee reduction, and the ordinance allows waiver or modification requests. Base rate for apartments: $10 per square foot of net new residential floor area. Planning and building permit fees still apply. The AHF NOFA scores host city land, fee waivers or inclusionary contributions toward its $1,000,000 or $20,000 per unit third-party commitment threshold.
set.next_deadline: Not applicable. Deed-restricted affordable units in unincorporated San Mateo County are exempt from the County affordable housing impact fee at permit; other County planning and building fees apply. Ask host cities about their own fee waivers.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: the cited inclusionary page has no fee waiver content. The County impact fee page and Resolution 074532 Exhibit C (smcgov.org/media/73946) show deed-restricted affordable units are exempt from the County affordable housing impact fee, contradicting the prior text that told users to budget full County fees. Program name still reads no countywide program; consider renaming to the impact fee exemption.

reason: Material: typical_award_size and next_deadline said to budget full County fees, but Resolution 074532 exempts deed-restricted affordable units from the County affordable housing impact fee.

set.per_unit_cap: Revenue and Taxation Code 214(g)(1)(C) caps the exemption at $20,000,000 of assessed value per taxpayer per fiscal year (single or multiple properties), and only where the exemption rests solely on the 90 percent lower income occupancy test for a property not owned by a limited partnership. Projects with tax-exempt bonds, government loans or grants (214(g)(1)(A)) or low-income housing tax credits (214(g)(1)(B)) are outside the cap; LP-owned projects with a nonprofit managing general partner must have tax credits or government financing to qualify (BOE Publication 149). Not a statewide cap.
set.prevailing_wage_basis: Property tax exemption; no construction funds are provided, so the exemption itself does not make a project public works.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: ACRE page lists BOE-267, 267-L, L-B (100% AMI worksheet), L1, L2, L3 (140% AMI over-income), L4 (100% AMI over-income), H, O and R and says BOE-267-A is omitted; Feb 15 deadline per Rev. and Tax. Code 255 and BOE Publication 149 (late claims: 90% relief if filed by Jan 1 of the next year, 85% after). The prior per_unit_cap described a statewide cap for LP projects; the statute applies it per taxpayer to non-LP claims under the 90% occupancy test.

reason: Material: per_unit_cap misdescribed the $20 million cap as a statewide aggregate for LP projects; Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)(1)(C) applies it per taxpayer only to non-LP claims qualifying solely on the 90 percent occupancy test.
